title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a base scheme. M is a rank-2 Azumaya algebra over S, i.e. a twisted form of Mat_2. G, SG, PG are the corresponding forms of GL2, SL2, PGL2. The page continues a proposition characterising 'regular' sections ρ of M (not necessarily invertible). Write v = det ρ and w = Tr ρ, so that Cayley–Hamilton gives ρ² = wρ − v.

Part of the list of equivalent conditions on the previous page:
- (a) ρ is a scalar on no fibre.
- (a') A_ρ = O_S + O_S ρ is locally a direct summand of M, free of rank 2. It is a commutative subalgebra.
- (b) Locally there is a cyclic vector e0, i.e. (e0, ρe0) is a basis of F.
- (b'') F is a locally monogenic O_S[T]-module, with T acting by ρ.
- (c) F_ρ ≅ O_S[T]/(T² − wT + v).

This page adds:
- (c') Locally there is a basis in which ρ is the companion matrix (0 −v; 1 w). These are exactly the bases (e0, e1 = ρe0).
- (c'') The same with the transposed companion matrix (0 1; −v w).
- (d) The commutant of ρ in M is exactly A_ρ, and this remains true after any base change S' → S.
- (d') The same on each fibre.

Proof sketch on the page:
- a ⇔ a' is linear algebra of locally direct summands.
- b ⇔ b' ⇔ b'' and b ⇒ a are trivial.
- a ⇒ b: on a fibre over a field, a non-scalar endomorphism has a non-eigenvector; lift it to a neighbourhood (Nakayama).
- b ⇔ c ⇔ c' are trivial.
- c' ⇔ c'' expresses that ρ is regular iff its transpose ᵗρ (acting on F^∨) is. This is immediate from form (a), since a matrix is scalar iff its transpose is.
- d ⇒ d' ⇒ a is trivial.
- What remains is b ⇒ d. The page breaks off: since the conditions are stable under base change, it suffices to check something (presumably the commutant computation in the cyclic basis).

Purpose. This is preparation for the next page: a criterion for solving the commutator equation [α, ρ] = ξ, i.e. αρα⁻¹ = ξρ, locally with α in G or SG. It holds iff ξρ is regular, det ξ = 1 and Tr ξρ = Tr ρ. The ambiguity in α is right multiplication by A_ρ^*. This feeds the analysis of the 'équation des lacets' in the GT / Longue Marche context, here for forms of GL2 over a base.
errors: The parenthetical after (3) appears to read ρe1 = −vρe0 − we0. The correct relation is ρe1 = ρ²e0 = wρe0 − v e0 = −v e0 + w e1. The matrix (3) itself is correct, with columns giving the images of the basis vectors. So this is a slip in the side remark only.

The proof of b ⇒ d is left unfinished at the bottom of the page. It is a routine argument: in a cyclic basis, an endomorphism commuting with ρ is determined by the image of e0, and this gives commutant = O_S[ρ] universally.

ideas.what: Characterisation of regular (cyclic) sections of a rank-2 Azumaya algebra: nowhere-scalar ⇔ local cyclic vector ⇔ F ≅ O_S[T]/(char poly) ⇔ local companion-matrix form ⇔ commutant = O_S[ρ] universally.
ideas.modern_name: Regular elements / cyclic vectors / companion matrix over a base; centraliser of regular elements (Steinberg–Kostant regularity in GL2 over a ring)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical linear algebra (Frobenius); over general bases folklore, cf. Steinberg and Kostant on regular elements, SGA3 for the group-scheme setting
ideas.where_published: Not in this form; related regular-element material appears in SGA3 (Exp. XIII–XIV)

ideas.what: Transpose duality: ρ is regular iff ᵗρ is, which gives the two companion forms (3) and (4).

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but standard linear algebra over a base: regular elements of rank-2 Azumaya algebras, cyclic vectors, companion matrices and commutants. It is preparatory to a commutator-equation criterion on the next page and contains nothing beyond folklore.
transcription_corrections: Side remark after (3): the intended correct formula is ρe1 = −v e0 + w e1. The manuscript appears to read '−vρe0 − we0', which is a slip, whether Grothendieck's or the transcriber's.
'(c") ∃ loc. sur [?]' most likely reads '∃ loc. Zar.', consistent with c').
'Commuting [?] le [?] pas chgt de base' likely reads something like 'Comme ... commute aux chgts de base, il suffit de voir que', i.e. a reduction by stability under base change.
'b⇔ c) ⇔ c')': the image shows a 'b' with an arrow written before c), consistent with the transcription.
